lines.en: Pushing through the Small Island's jungle, Jang Hayoung recalled Kim Dokja's words.
—You're the ace in the hole for this scenario.
Before the scenario began, Kim Dokja had called Jang Hayoung aside and said that.
But hearing such words out of nowhere had only left Hayoung bewildered.
‘······He never paid me any attention before.’

It hurt. Even allowing for the difference in how long he had known his other companions, Kim Dokja had been far too neglectful. Three years had passed since the [Revolutionary Game] and [Demon King Selection] scenarios. Throughout that time, Jang Hayoung had felt left out.
How to put it? Like being repeatedly excluded from the major scenarios.
—Why don't you ask me to join <Kim Dokja’s Company>?
That hurt most of all.
Hayoung wanted to ask.
Why Kim Dokja never suggested that Hayoung join his nebula.
Surely he hadn't forgotten······.
[The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘Don't trust Kim Dokja too much.’]
“Be quiet.”
[The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘He's only using you.’]
Perhaps that really was true.
Kim Dokja was the most pragmatic person Jang Hayoung knew.
Even so, Hayoung answered,
“Kim Dokja isn't like that. Why do you hate him so much?”
[The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ asks, ‘Do you want to become close to him?’]
“Well, it'd be nice······ We haven't talked much lately.”
[The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ asks, ‘Why? Do you like him?’]
“Who said I like him?”
Jang Hayoung answered brusquely and pouted.
“The one I like is the ‘Demon King of Salvation’.”
[The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ glares at you. ‘They're the same person.’]
“They're different! Anyway, I just want to get along with everyone.”
[The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ sighs. ‘Even if he kills you someday?’]
“Why would you say something so ominous?”
Come to think of it, the [Unidentifiable Wall] had always disliked Kim Dokja. From their first meeting until now, without exception.
“Stop getting in my way. Last time, I was the only one who didn't get a ‘Giant Story’ because of you.”
The Giant Story that had crowned <Gigantomachia> with victory, 「Torch That Swallowed the Myth」.
Watching that scene on a screen, Jang Hayoung had felt overwhelmed, moved, and, in the end, sad and alone.
Hayoung thought that was where they should have been, too.
Should have thrown themselves onto those burning flames, too.
Should have become part of that enormous Story.
But couldn't.
[The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘Trust people and you'll only be disappointed again. You've experienced enough of that in your past life.’]
Hayoung lacked confidence.
What if the sacred flame went out when she jumped in?
What if her intervention ruined the ‘Giant Story’?
······What if Kim Dokja didn't want her to join in?
Jang Hayoung was different from the other companions.
She was a resident of the Demon Realm who had crossed over to Earth, not a companion who had fought alongside Kim Dokja from the first scenario.
So she couldn't say she wanted to go with them.
An insurmountable wall stood between them. A wall that kept her from drawing closer to them, however hard she tried. Jang Hayoung didn't have their shared history.
“This way! Just a little farther!”
“Heewon-ssi, give Gilyoung to me. I'll carry him.”
“It's fine! I still have that much stamina.”
Voices came from the distant undergrowth. Jang Hayoung instinctively hid behind a tree. A man and woman covered in wounds were running, each carrying a child on their back. Hayoung knew them, too.
Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung.
Monsters were chasing them. Five or six orcs, followed by two trolls.
From their direction, they seemed to be crossing the field toward the smoke. A bad choice. Because far more terrifying monsters than orcs or trolls lay in their path.
At this rate, the companions would be wiped out.
Jang Hayoung instinctively clenched her fist and stood.
More precisely, she tried to stand.
[The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘Don't save them.’]
“What? What bullshit is that?”
[The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘If they die here, you can become Kim Dokja's only companion.’]

Almost simultaneously, Jung Heewon tripped over a stone and fell. She and Lee Gilyoung rolled across the ground. Right behind them, the pursuing orcs grinned and raised their glaives. It was too late to dodge.
Jung Heewon shouted.
“Gilyoung! Run!”
Watching the descending glaive, Jang Hayoung thought.
Perhaps the [Unidentifiable Wall] was right.
If they died here······.
—Thank you.
What flashed through her mind then was a conversation with Kim Dokja just before coming here.
—For what?
—What you told me back then.
With his usual pale face, Kim Dokja murmured.
—You said that even if the person beyond the wall can't hear you······ you should still try leaving something on it.
Jang Hayoung was puzzled.
Had she said that? When?
······Had she been drunk?
Kim Dokja continued.
—So that's what I'm doing. Just as you said, maybe someday someone will look at the traces on that wall.
She sees Jung Heewon squeezing her eyes shut beneath the falling glaive.
Lee Hyunsung shouting, Lee Gilyoung covering Jung Heewon.
By the time she came to her senses, Jang Hayoung was already running.
[Your new attribute prepares to bloom.]
Her fist shot out like lightning.
The orc's glaive snapped like a sorghum stalk beneath the transcendent's fist.
Jung Heewon was looking up at her, wide-eyed.
Looking down at her, Jang Hayoung thought.
‘How stupid······.’
Kim Dokja would never know how she felt.
The ‘Demon King of Salvation’ was a demon king, not a god. He probably had no interest in what she did or how she did it.
But just because her feelings couldn't reach him didn't mean they had never existed.
Standing protectively before the companions, Jang Hayoung said,
“Leave it to me from here.”
It wasn't too late to begin building a history now.
She still had plenty of time.
I opened my eyes, exhaling.
[‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’ Stage 3 has ended.]
[‘Third-Person Observer's Viewpoint’ has ended.]
Fortunately, Jang Hayoung had met my companions. I'd been anxious that their meeting might be delayed, but thankfully, things had gone according to plan.
Now that they had met Hayoung, my companions would be safe.
I rose stiffly and checked the messages floating before me again.
[As a reward for clearing the ‘hidden scenario’, you have gained permission to use the skill, ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’.]
Normally, skills couldn't be used on ‘Reincarnation Island’. But things changed a little once you completed the ‘Hidden Scenario—Survival Game’.
[The exclusive skill, ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’, will be fixed at its minimum level.]
[A system error has occurred. This skill has no concept of levels.]
[This skill is unaffected by ‘first-generation probability’.]
At first, I'd wondered whether permission to use [Bookmark] would be better. But thinking about it, [Bookmark] was a skill that borrowed other people's skills anyway.
In other words, even with permission to use it, [Bookmark] would be useless unless I also gained permission to use those other people's skills.
This island really had too many restrictions, but it couldn't be helped.
What I had to gain here was more important than skills.
Lee Jihye's voice came from far away.
“Great-grandmasteeer!”
It was already the second day.
Lee Jihye had been following One Invincible Fist Yoo Hoseong everywhere.
“Great-grandmaster! Teach me that Story!”
Even when Yoo Hoseong fed the cattle.
“Just one passage! I can learn it really well.”
Even while he did laundry or chopped wood, Lee Jihye pestered him.
“How did you do that yesterday? You just thrust your fist out and all their heads burst!”
Of course, Yoo Hoseong said nothing.
I had expected that ‘Story Control’ wouldn't be easy to learn. Even Kyrgios and the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had taken a long time to learn this technique from him.
Story Control.

It was the name of a pure technique, neither a skill nor a stigma. ‘Ways of Survival’ offered various explanations, but so much of it was vague that even I didn't really understand. That did worry me.
[The Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, growls.]
······I needed to do something about this bastard, fast.
Yoo Hoseong first lost his temper that evening.
“Stop following me. Why am I your great-grandmaster?”
“Because······ you're my master's master's master!”
Listening to her answer with that bright smile, I thought she had a point.
Lee Jihye's master was Yoo Joonghyuk, whose master was the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, whose master was One Invincible Fist Yoo Hoseong.
Glaring at Lee Jihye, Yoo Hoseong sighed and said,
“This isn't something you can learn just because I teach you. People used to the system like you won't get anywhere, however long you train.”
“But you taught the grandmasters!”
“They were transcendents without sponsors. Different from you.”
A cold rejection.
“But you never know! I'll do whatever you tell me, exactly as you say!”
“That attitude is wrong to begin with. I'm saying this isn't something you learn by ‘doing as you're told’! Haven't you felt anything following me around for two days?”
As befitted Yoo Joonghyuk's grandmaster, Yoo Hoseong gave an obnoxious smile (they even had the same surname).
In truth, I knew.
That Yoo Hoseong had been testing us all along.
“Have you heard nothing here?”
At his words, Lee Jihye and I looked around at the same time.
A burly man cleaning up pig dung glared back at me, asking what I was looking at.
[The Story, ‘Master of Cleaning Up Dung’, resolves to enjoy another day.]
A woman harvesting crops was drinking makgeolli and humming a song.
[The Story, ‘Master of Work Songs’, hums as it helps its owner work.]
An old man chopping wood sighed deeply and sat down on his carrying frame.
[The Story, ‘Thousand-Year Woodcutter’, says young people these days have no respect for their elders.]
They weren't particularly impressive Stories.
Stories created by merely cleaning up animal dung, singing work songs, or chopping wood. Yet they were of a different kind from the other Stories I knew.
I sensed a strange creative force (造化) at work in those Stories.
Something different from Stories that sought only great power or tried to rule their owners. An ensemble created by a being and a Story spending long years together.
Yoo Hoseong said,
“Something that takes ten, a hundred, a thousand years of training to yield a single sentence. That is a ‘true Story’.”
A true Story.
An interesting expression.
“You have Stories of your own, don't you? Train those well. There's no point trying to learn other Stories now.”
“But······ we can't become as strong as you with these, Great-grandmaster.”
“That depends on what you do. What matters is looking closely at your Stories.”
“Looking closely?”
“When a story is too large, it can keep you from seeing where that story is going.”
Come to think of it, I had heard something similarly cryptic before.
When was that? When I was learning [Way of the Wind] from Lycaon?
Thinking about various things, I suddenly grew worried.
······Could I properly learn Story Control when I couldn't even learn [Way of the Wind]?
I really didn't need another lecture about talent this and talent that.
Sighing, Yoo Hoseong spoke again.
“Ugh, you damned brats. I'll explain just once.”
At those words, Lee Jihye sat before him like a well-behaved student.
I, too, sidled closer to listen.
“What do you think a ‘Story’ is?”
Lee Jihye shifted her gaze as she thought, then answered.
“Um······ a story?”
“Pathetic.”
“Don't just scold us. Explain properly!”
“I'll have to start with the basics.”
Clicking his tongue, Yoo Hoseong raised his left hand.
“What do you call this?”
“······Your left hand?”
Yoo Hoseong raised his other hand.
“And this one?”
“Your right hand.”
“And what do you get when you put the two together?”
After thinking hard, Lee Jihye answered.
“······Both hands?”
Then a Story answered in Yoo Hoseong's place.
[The Story, ‘Ambidextrous Boxer’, is delighted.]
“Yes. They're connected by the words ‘both hands’. A ‘relationship’ that many beings call by that name, perceive that way, and understand in much the same way.”
Lee Jihye looked blank. As though she understood, but didn't.
As if he had expected that, Yoo Hoseong continued.
“Then what would you call this?”
Picking up a fallen branch in his left hand, he asked,
“One is a left hand, and one is a branch. What should we call them together?”
“Um······ a left hand holding a branch? Or······ a left hand and a branch······.”
Neither name felt satisfying.
“It isn't easy to name them, is it? Do you know why?”
Lee Jihye shook her head.
Yoo Hoseong said,
“Because there's no proper ‘relationship’ between the two. Whether you say a left hand and a branch, or a left hand holding a branch, something doesn't quite fit. They're awkward together.”
Holding the branch like a dart, he threw it at a distant tree. It flew swiftly and lodged in the trunk. It looked as natural as if it had always been a branch of that tree.
“A ‘Story’ closes that awkward distance. It connects the world's most distant things. If you want to control Stories, first understand them properly.”
An explanation I almost understood, but not quite. Watching the branch embedded in the tree, Lee Jihye blinked blankly.
I carefully picked up a stone lying on the ground.
A power connecting the world's most distant things······ Difficult.
Watching me, Yoo Hoseong clicked his tongue and said,

“You idiot. I was only giving an example. You don't create a relationship and a Story just by grabbing anything! Only after spending long years closing the distance between the material and yourself······!”
Then, the next moment, something strange happened.
Bzzzzzt!
[The abundant probability of the first generation responds to your actions.]
[The Story material feels friendly toward you.]
The stone in my hand was looking up at me, seemingly happy.
[The Story, ‘The Stone and I’, begins its story.]
Staring at me in a daze, Yoo Hoseong asked with trembling lips,
“What on earth are you?”
The stone quivered on my hand as though alive.
[You have acquired a new Story!]
[The Story, ‘The Stone and I’, wants to continue its story.]
This was a first for me, too.
A Story had formed just because I touched a stone?
All sorts of complicated theories flashed through my head, but no suitable answer came to mind.
[First-generation probability swirls around you.]
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ is currently very thin.]
If anything looked suspicious, it was those two system messages.
Glaring at me suspiciously, Yoo Hoseong said,
“······I see. You're a reincarnator, too. Aren't you?”
He seemed to have formed a completely wrong theory about me in the meantime.
“Were you stoned to death in your past life? So that stone······.”
“No.”
“Aha, you're a stonehead. That explains why it was a stone—”
Without a word, I picked up the branch Yoo Hoseong had thrown.
[The Story material responds sensitively to you.]
[The Story, ‘Kim Dokja is Like a Branch’, begins its story!]
To the openmouthed Yoo Hoseong, I tried speaking like a humble young Murim talent.
“With respect, I'm not quite that thickheaded.”
Beside me, Lee Jihye glared as though I was insufferable.
Eyes bulging, Yoo Hoseong shouted.
“Here, try holding this too!”
I accepted the flower he held out.
[The Story material takes a liking to you.]
[The Story, ‘Kim Dokja with a Flower’, begins its story!]
Yoo Hoseong kept handing me things that could serve as Story material, and I accepted them one after another.
[The Story material becomes curious about you!]
[The Story material becomes curious about you!]
By the time my surroundings were full of singing flowers and stones, Yoo Hoseong finally reached a decision after much thought.
“······Hold me.”
“Where?”
“Here. Put your hand on my shoulder.”
Yoo Hoseong's blazing eyes.
I understood his anger. As he'd said, those ‘true Stories’ that took ten, a hundred, a thousand years to form one line were budding from me far too easily······ Of course he would be furious.
“If you insist······ Excuse me.”
Sighing, I put a hand on Yoo Hoseong's shoulder.
······How could a child's shoulder be this hard?
Yoo Hoseong said,
“No particular change. Limited to inanimate objects? Hmm······.”
[The character, ‘Yoo Hoseong’, takes a slight liking to you.]
Startled, he shook my hand off and backed away.
“Wh-what have you done······?”
Then a message sounded in my ears.
[You have acquired the Story, ‘Person Who is Loved by All’.]
While Yoo Hoseong was reeling in shock, the other villagers took an interest in me.
“It's been a while since I've seen talent this insane.”
“Well, what a rare fellow······ Are you sure you're from outside?”
“Would you be interested in cattle feed, too?”
Feeling bewildered, I accepted the cattle feed the woman handed me.
The human Kim Dokja.
In nearly thirty years of muddling through life, I thought this was the first time I'd attracted attention for something this good.
I······ had talent?
「(You certainly do, Dokja-ssi. ······You spent over ten years reading a novel like this all the way to the end.)」
Yoo Sangah sounded a little tired, perhaps because her work as a librarian had been hard lately.
‘······Do you think it's connected to reading the novel?’
「(I can't think of another explanation.)」
‘But nothing like this has ever happened before······.’
Thinking about it, that wasn't entirely true.
Some characters had liked me from the moment they saw me.
「(Could it be connected to the ‘Wall’ becoming thinner?)」
Listening to her, I thought that was possible. I didn't know exactly why, but perhaps the [Fourth Wall]'s weakened functions had brought the world and me closer together.
······Then how far did this ability extend?
Looking beside me, I saw Lee Jihye clutching a branch and muttering to herself, her pride apparently hurt.
I poked her arm with a finger.
“Urgh!”
Startled, Lee Jihye snapped.
“Are you crazy, ajusshi? How dare you touch me with that dung-covered finger······!”
Apparently it didn't work on her. Then, let's see······.
I tried poking Cheok Jungyeong's shoulder. He was sitting cross-legged right beside me, too.
“Is that a challenge?”
“No.”
······It didn't work on him, either.
Then how on earth did it work?
However much I thought, I couldn't understand the mechanism behind my talent.
“That really is some damned talent. There's no other explanation.”
The speaker was Yoo Hoseong, who had spent a long time lost in thought.
Ominous anger showed on his clear, youthful face.
Striding toward me with a child's steps, he spoke.
“You may not know this, but I hate fortuitous encounters more than anything. Especially people like you who get things easily, without effort. Those I despise most.”
That was the sort of man One Invincible Fist Yoo Hoseong was.
A martial artist who liked tenacious people, and cherished those who strove to overcome insurmountable talent.
To him, someone like me must have seemed guilty of high treason for insulting the first generation through sheer talent.
“······Today, for the first time, I'll go against my convictions.”
Huh?
“I will teach you ‘Story Control’.”
I didn't know why Yoo Hoseong had changed his mind.
But one thing was certain: he had seen some potential in me.
As though determined to leave behind the greatest disciple of his life, he tormented me day and night from then on.
“Phenomena and truth are not the same. Using a Story properly means understanding phenomena in your own language.”
“Solid ground from which to leap into abstraction. That is the detail (細部) you must build in your Story.”
······And so on.
It was such incomprehensible nonsense that I wondered whether I'd be better off rereading ‘Ways of Survival’.
Peeling and eating a tangerine a villager had brought, I nodded earnestly for the time being.
“You idiot. You look as though you haven't understood a thing.”
“My apologies.”
“If you don't understand, you needn't force yourself. Not everyone acquires Story Control the same way.”
“······Then what do you want me to do?”
I got flicked on the forehead.
“Impudent brat. The way you speak is your first problem. You lack respect for your elders.”
“First, you must learn to listen.”
“I don't think I could be listening any more carefully.”
“I mean listen to what your Stories say!”
······What my Stories said?
Had something like that appeared in ‘Ways of Survival’?
“You already have the talent to communicate with Stories. The talent to listen to their feelings and words.”
Come to think of it, that was certainly true.
I didn't know when it began, but I had become able to read what Stories wanted. As though they were people.
“But I want to control Stories, not make small talk with them.”
“Stories cannot be controlled.”
So said the man teaching Story Control.
“Can you control your own thoughts?”
“Of course. They're my thoughts······.”
“Then think of nothing for the next five minutes.”
I nodded as though that would be easy.
Don't think, don't think······.
Damn it. I was thinking, ‘Don't think.’
I tried hard to run away from my imagination, but it wasn't easy.
In less than five minutes, a great many things happened in my head.

For instance, Yoo Joonghyuk turning into a beautiful girl for some implausible reason and slicing demon kings to death, or Han Sooyoung suffering an equally unexplained mental breakdown and declaring, “Kim Dokja-nim, I really am sorry for plagiarizing back then”······.
I raised both hands and admitted defeat.
“Halfwit.”
[The Story, ‘Demon King of Salvation’, grins at you.]
“From today, that is your task. Listen to your Stories.”
“Don't be afraid. However enormous a Story may be, it's still a Story you built.”
Turning away as he said this, Yoo Hoseong wore the expression of a teacher for the first time.
“Stories sometimes try to rule us, but sometimes they show us the way.”
From that day, I began training in ‘Story Control’.
More precisely, I practiced listening to my Stories' voices.
[The Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, finds your attention bothersome.]

The Stories found this behavior unfamiliar, but as a day passed, then two, they began opening up little by little. After listening for who knew how long, I began to hear the voices of Stories that had held back from expressing their feelings until now.
[The Story, ‘King of a Kingless World’, says it was really fun back then.]
A Story tells a story, and I listen to that story.
Once more, the story becomes a memory we built together.
The Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword's starlight embroidered across the sky, and the exhilarating moment of shattering the [Absolute Throne].
Yes, it really was fun back then.
You were my ‘first Story’.
[The Story, ‘One Who Opposes the Extraordinary’, says that returnee was a real headache.]
Right. That bastard Myung Ilsang was really troublesome.
I nearly died even with Yoo Joonghyuk and Han Sooyoung there.
[The Story, ‘One Who Hunted the King of Disasters’, misses the taste of snake liquor.]
[The Story, ‘One Who Killed an Outer God’, asks whether you remember this too.]
With each new remark, I sank into memories not yet fully ripened.
At the same time, I felt impatient, knowing I couldn't linger here too long.
Han Sooyoung, Yoo Joonghyuk, Anna Croft······.
They would pursue endings different from mine, and might already be knocking on the next scenario's door.
[The Story, ‘Demon King of Salvation’, says you must not run away anymore.]
I focused on the story again.
At some point, as more and more Story voices poured out, I found it hard to distinguish reality from fiction. My sense of space and time blurred. I couldn't tell whether I was inside the Stories,
or listening to their stories in reality.
[The Story, ‘Silver Screen Revolutionary’, hungers for a new revolution.]
Yes, I'm sorry.
I've neglected you for too long.
[The Story, ‘Gourmet Association Heretic’, complains of hunger!]
[The Story, ‘Miracle Gambler’, says to play another big game.]
From time to time, dreamlike scenes flashed past.
—Dokja-ssi. We really did almost die. Do you know that?
—Ajusshiii!
My companions' voices, faintly audible somewhere.
—······Wow, that's unfair. You started training all by yourself?
—Let's learn too, right away! Who do we go to?
Listening to those voices, I think.
If this is really a dream, it's such a sweet one.
—······Why aren't I getting a Story? I heard Dokja-hyung got one by doing this.
—Take your hand off, Lee Gilyoung.
—You get away, Shin Yoosung.
Through the dream, I heard the children earnestly muttering things like “Ajusshi and I” and “Dokja-hyung and Lee Gilyoung”.
I didn't know what they would do with Stories like those, but······.
[The Giant Story, ‘Demon Realm's Spring’, watches your story with you.]
Why was that? Without my realizing it, the children's voices had warmed my heart. In my hazy vision, countless Stories watched the scene alongside me.
[The Story, ‘Person Who is Loved by an Archangel’, likes your story.]
[The Story, ‘King of a Kingless World’, watches the children.]
[The Story, ‘Giant’s Liberator’, looks fondly at your companions.]
All these Stories resemble me, and I, in turn, resemble them all.
Then that one off by itself over there must surely be part of us, too.
[The Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, turns away from you.]
I say,
‘Stop sulking and come here.’
But it didn't answer.
It had threatened the other Stories with its mountain-sized bulk, but now it sat curled up with its back turned.
Head bowed, like a child reading something.
Perhaps I recognize that back. A small child wholly absorbed in a story of their own.
But as always, a ‘Story’ cannot exist alone.
I approached it carefully from behind and said,
‘That looks interesting.’
Startled, 「Torch That Swallowed the Myth」 turned to me and swelled.
With its now-enormous body, the Story glared at me.
Strangely, I wasn't afraid of it.
It was a Story. And every Story flows somewhere.
‘Where do you want to go?’
Unable to answer my question readily, it merely opened and closed its mouth.
It probably couldn't answer. I knew how that felt.
‘Come with me.’
Slowly, I open my mouth and speak.
The ■■ I desire for all my stories.
The Story asks,
「What lies at the end of all those stories?」
‘I don't know either. But at least we won't be alone.’
[The Story, ‘Hell of Eternity’, watches you.]
And a moment later, I felt the Stories winding around my fingertips. My body, swept along by waves of stories, gradually grew heavy. Slowly, I opened my eyes.
I couldn't tell how much time had passed.
My legs were numb. Looking down, I found Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung sleeping peacefully against my knees. This was no Story. Children with real flesh and blood.
I gently stroked their heads.
[The Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, listens to your story.]
At last, I was ready to leave for the next scenario.
At that moment, the sole survivor of the 331st island was moving toward the next scenario.
[You have slaughtered every participant on the island.]
[You are the sole survivor of the 331st island.]
[You have qualified to enter the next scenario.]
A fluttering black coat, and [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] gleaming on his back.

Looking at the portal to the next scenario, Yoo Joonghyuk recalled the sinister being he had met just before coming here. An Outer God whose identity even he, now in his third round, couldn't discern.
—I cannot tell you the entire revelation. Even for me, that would violate ‘probability’ too greatly. But······ I can give you this much. That should make it a reasonably fair fight.
When he turned on his smartphone, a text file appeared.
『Han Sooyoung—Record of the 1863rd Round (Part I).』
Stepping toward the portal, Yoo Joonghyuk turned to the first page of a story he did not know.
Two weeks had passed since I reached the village.
Once my Stories settled into place, I immediately began preparing for the next scenario.

「‘Reincarnation Island’ broadly comprises three islands. The ‘Small Island’, where first-generation Story probability operates. The ‘Middle Island’, where second-generation Story probability operates. And finally, the ‘Main Island’, where third-generation Story probability operates······.」
Unlike on the ‘Small Island’, I would have to confront constellations in earnest from the ‘Middle Island’ onward.
Beings who had survived this realistic first-generation probability would be waiting for me there.
[The Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, urges you to hurry up.]
One of them was still throwing tantrums, but I thought I'd reined it in enough.
Yoo Hoseong had said that Stories sometimes tried to rule their users, but also showed them the way forward.
[The Giant Story, ‘Demon Realm's Spring’, awaits your choice.]
These Stories would go on living alongside me.
We would create stories together, and shape them into yet more Stories.
“Heewon-ssi, I'm glad you're safe.”
“Can't you try a different greeting? I really did almost die this time.”
Apparently, my companions had arrived about a week after I began Story Control training. They'd gotten lost near the island's outskirts, delaying their arrival further.
Looking around, I asked,
“Where are the others?”
“They're all training.”
After we walked a little, I saw the children, Lee Hyunsung, and Jang Hayoung sitting cross-legged. Their expressions suggested the training wasn't easy.
Naturally.
Story Control training took at least two months. Even Yoo Joonghyuk in the original novel, with all his incredible talent, had had to waste three whole weeks on it······.
I quietly examined my companions' Stories.
[The Story, ‘Kim Dokja’s Company Code of Conduct’, writhes painfully.]
[The Story, ‘One Who Hears the Voices of Monsters’, groans.]

The <0th Murim>, known only in legend.

Reincarnation Island. The <Star Stream>'s living museum. In exchange for living eternally on the island, its reincarnators were cursed never to leave it.

So that he could take the remaining half himself.
“Don't you think it's time you did the talking yourself?”
Ripples spread through Yoo Hoseong's widened eyes.

Wishing that his technique would change the island, change the ‘Great War of Saints and Demons’, and finally change the <Star Stream>.

[The Story, ‘World's Oldest Farmer’, sees you off.]

Stories remember the moment when the world's most distant things meet and part.

—The ‘island's owner’ may take an interest in you. You should be careful.

No, please be bound by personal ties.
